races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Maiden
Hotel Killarney Maiden

runners_data.name: Coul Dreamer
runners_data.note: W. McCreery's five-year-old has a fair piece of form at this trip on good ground — including a third at 8f on good — and is genuinely a horse who wants to come from off the pace, though the map shows him in midfield because the hold-up berths in this race are already oversubscribed.|

runners_data.name: Desert Swing
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and stylistically unknown, this Andrew Kinirons runner gives very little away; Robbie Colgan's booking is the main angle, and until this horse shows us its hand at the start, its influence on the pace map remains genuinely uncertain.|

runners_data.name: Medadthebookie
runners_data.note: Edward Buckley's six-year-old has a consistent tendency to fade in the finish and has returned figures of 6, 9, 11, 9, 11 in recent outings — the form figures tell a clear story of a horse that struggles to land a blow at the business end, regardless of pace shape.|

runners_data.name: Mischievous Fun
runners_data.note: The trainer-rider combination of Andrew Slattery is intriguing at 2/34 over 14 days, but this four-year-old's three career runs have all ended in fades — finishing 6th, 12th, and 15th — and dropping to a mile from further is not an obvious solution based on available evidence.|

runners_data.name: Sron Na Caise
runners_data.note: K.J. Condon's four-year-old has placed at ten furlongs and wears a visor today for the first time, which could sharpen her early effort; by inclination she wants to race deep into the field, but the crowded hold-up division means W.J. Lee may need to compromise her position.|

runners_data.name: Tyraxes
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy is a major positive for Denis Hogan's horse, who has shown some ability at this distance; his true nature is that of a hold-up runner, though with several closers in this field he may find himself unable to get as far back as he ideally wants, and the tongue-piece and 63-day absence add further puzzle pieces.|

runners_data.name: Wild Sapphire
runners_data.note: D.K. Weld's four-year-old is the lone confirmed pace-setter here, with Chris Hayes able to control every fraction unchallenged; the tongue-tie is noted, she has placed on good ground before, and 96 days off is the one query, though Weld horses often reappear fresh and ready.|

runners_data.name: Dolly Hello
runners_data.note: Ben Coen takes over for Ross O'Sullivan on this lightly-raced filly returning after 260 days off, which is the dominant concern — she has placed at seven furlongs on good ground and drops back in trip today, but the layoff demands respect before confidence grows.|

races.paceDynamic: Wild Sapphire is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, Chris Hayes can dictate a measured, unchallenged gallop from the front on the Dermot Weld-trained four-year-old. The pace will be honest but controlled, with Wild Sapphire able to choose her own fractions and potentially steal a decisive advantage turning for home. Dolly Hello and Desert Swing, both unquantified in style, could slot prominently and offer token pressure, but neither is likely to seriously dispute the lead. This shape strongly favours the front-runner and anything racing close to the pace in the first two or three, as hold-up horses will need a stronger gallop to make up ground on a flat, one-mile track. The field carries significantly more hold-up runners than the race can accommodate at the rear — Tyraxes, Coul Dreamer, and Sron Na Caise are true hold-up types but have been redistributed to midfield on the map because they cannot all get their preferred rearward berth; in practice, Wild Sapphire is virtually certain to secure the rail and dictate.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sapphire Controls Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Wild Sapphire is allowed to bowl along unchallenged and sets a sustainable pace that holds the field in its wake.
scenarios.body: Wild Sapphire dictates throughout, with Chris Hayes able to conserve energy through the middle part of the race before kicking clear under the one-furlong pole; the flat Killarney track offers no hiding place for hold-up horses needing late cover. Prominent types close to the pace — including any unexposed runners who slot handily — are ideally positioned to pick off tiring rivals for the minor places.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Wild Sapphire sets a pace that is just quick enough to string out the field but leaves something for a prominent chaser to collar her inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A horse settled just off the leader through the early fractions conserves enough energy to reel in Wild Sapphire as she ties up, with Dolly Hello — stepping back to a more suitable trip and carrying a lighter weight — ideally placed to swoop from a handy position. Tyraxes, who has shown a turn of foot at this distance on good ground, could also emerge as a threat if Oisin Murphy positions him closer than his natural hold-up profile suggests.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Storms Home
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is deceptively strong and Wild Sapphire fades dramatically in the final two furlongs, leaving a gap for a finisher coming from off the pace.
scenarios.body: Coul Dreamer or Sron Na Caise, both genuine hold-up types who have shown ability to finish well when the race truly truly truly tests stamina, would be the chief beneficiaries, though both are racing at least partially out of their natural role given the redistribution in this field. The scenario requires the pace to be materially stronger than expected, which is a low-probability event given Wild Sapphire's unchallenged lead.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — No Clear Shape
scenarios.trigger: If Desert Swing or another unquantified runner contests the lead aggressively, turning the race into a genuine test of pace and breaking the expected front-runner scenario.
scenarios.body: With the going unknown and pace scenario scrambled, runners with tactical versatility — those able to race prominently or sit midfield — would be best placed to exploit any collapse at the front. This is a low-probability outcome but is made slightly plausible by the presence of two stylistically unknown runners in Desert Swing and Dolly Hello, whose intentions from the gate are unclear.

watchPoints.text: Watch Wild Sapphire's early gallop — if Chris Hayes sends her clear and the opening fractions are truly comfortable, the front-runner becomes very difficult to peg back on this flat mile track.

Desert Swing's stylistic unknown status means Robbie Colgan could choose to press Wild Sapphire for the lead from the gates, which would fundamentally alter the race shape — monitor the early exchanges closely.

Dolly Hello's 260-day absence is a significant red flag; even with Ben Coen aboard, a horse returning from that length of layoff can be ring-rusty at a crucial moment, particularly in the closing stages.

Tyraxes, Coul Dreamer, and Sron Na Caise are all genuine hold-up horses forced to compromise their positions — if any of them gets further back than the midfield map position suggests, they will need a strong late pace that this race is unlikely to provide.

Mischievous Fun and Medadthebookie have both shown a persistent tendency to fade in the finish across multiple recent runs — neither is likely to improve that pattern in a race where the pace may not be strong enough to suit closers.

races.name: Irish Examiner Handicap

runners_data.name: Sunrise Angel
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist who fades late per flags — Andrew Slattery trains and rides, 64 days off the track is a concern, and sim-going record on good ground is sparse (3/7 with zero wins or places); needs a pace injection that this race is unlikely to provide.

runners_data.name: Zheleznaya Dama
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy is a significant jockey booking for Brendan Duke's filly, who was out just three days ago — fitness is not in doubt; six good-ground runs suggest she handles the surface, and her hold-up tag is less extreme than most in this field, giving her the option to track closer than her label suggests.

runners_data.name: Wicklow Gap
runners_data.note: Gary Carroll rides for Gavin Cromwell and the tongue-tie is noted; the nine-run form string on good ground at this trip (4/8) shows some aptitude but finishing positions of 9-12-4-9-9 in the past five suggest inconsistency rather than a horse on a progressive curve.

runners_data.name: Concaire
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner in the field who sets the entire race up from the front — Ben Coen's experience of lead roles is an asset here; the STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) is a minor technical flag but this horse's natural style is precisely what this position requires, so it can be read with less discount than usual.

runners_data.name: De Songbird
runners_data.note: Sadhbh Tormey takes the seven-pound claim for T.G. McCourt's filly, who has two good-ground starts to reference (one a fifth at 8f) and no win or place on similar going; running in a hold-up role in a race where the late-running lanes will be congested is problematic.

runners_data.name: Sayonara
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery also saddles this one, run just three days ago, and the form string shows a horse that has struggled to place in recent sprints — its true hold-up style is squeezed into a midfield slot on the map because the rear is oversubscribed, which only adds to the challenge of finding a clean run.

runners_data.name: Tavarua
runners_data.note: W.J. Lee partners this K.J. Condon-trained three-year-old who has dropped from 10f to 1m — the trip shortening could be positive, but the genuine hold-up profile means it is mapped midfield under the redistribution flag, and four finishes between sixth and fifteenth suggest limited scope for improvement without a strongly run race.

runners_data.name: Wingit
runners_data.note: Patrick Magee's yard has been active (4/10 in 14 days) and the tongue-tie is on; Wingit has nine starts yielding finishes mostly in sixth-to-twelfth range, and its natural deep-closer style will be compromised by a steady pace — the redistribution into midfield reflects the crowded rear, not an opportunity.

runners_data.name: Six Wings
runners_data.note: Paul Flynn has sent this filly out recently (4/26 in 14 days) and the tongue-tie/blinkers combination is notable; five consecutive finishes on good ground in the 6th-to-13th range with zero wins or places makes this a horse that needs things to go right, which the race shape does not promise.

runners_data.name: Stonyfalls
runners_data.note: Killian Leonard rides for Paul Traynor in what is a rare runner for that yard; third at 8f on good ground is the standout piece of recent form and is exactly the distance and surface here — the redistribution into midfield is circumstantial rather than a reflection of the horse's true best position.

runners_data.name: Garryowen Green
runners_data.note: Chris Hayes is a notable booking for Andrew McNamara's gelding, 33 days off, and the tongue-tie stays on; four runs show a horse that struggles to get competitive (9th, 9th, 9th, 14th) and the 9f-heavy history raises mild stamina questions about whether the mile is even its best trip.

runners_data.name: Ramair
runners_data.note: Shay Wallace's seven-pound claim is significant for a yard with no runners in 14 days; the historical form at 8f on similar going (3rd and 5th) gives a small positive signal, but 70 days off the track is the key flag — the redistribution into midfield understates its true rearward tendency.

runners_data.name: Beau Army
runners_data.note: Declan McDonogh is an upgrade in the saddle for Adrian McGuinness, who has one winner from 27 in the past fortnight; the form includes a second at 8f on soft and a fourth at 7f on good, and of the redistributed hold-up horses this one has the best evidence of placing ability on a related surface.

runners_data.name: Cause I Like You
runners_data.note: Wesley Joyce takes three pounds off for Michael Mulvany — second at 8f on good ground and a fourth at 8f on similar give tangible evidence that the trip and surface suit; genuine hold-up profile pushed into a midfield slot on the map, but the race shape must open up for this horse to deliver its best.

races.paceDynamic: Concaire is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 14-runner mile handicap and, with no other genuine lead-seeking type to challenge for early position, Ben Coen can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front — this is a classic lone-pace scenario where the fractions are unlikely to be truly searching. The overwhelming majority of the field are classified hold-up horses, but the field holds considerably more genuine hold-up and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear: Sayonara, Tavarua, Wingit, Six Wings, Stonyfalls, Garryowen Green, Ramair, Beau Army and Cause I Like You are all true hold-up horses redistributed into midfield on the map, meaning the back half of the field will be densely packed and genuine last-to-first closers will face serious traffic and positional problems. With Concaire able to bowl along at a comfortable clip unchallenged, those who can race close enough to the pace — in the prominent or midfield-tracking bracket — will be ideally positioned to pounce as the hold-up brigade gets shuffled and blocked. This race shape strongly favours horses that can track within three or four lengths of Concaire through the race and unleash their finish from a handy position, rather than deep closers who need a searching gallop to bring them into it.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Concaire Controls, Trackerswin
scenarios.trigger: If Concaire leads unchallenged and sets a steady-to-moderate tempo, horses tracking in second to fifth position inherit the ideal racing position.
scenarios.body: Concaire's uncontested lead means the pace is dictated entirely on his terms, compressing the field and eliminating any significant gaps for late closers to exploit; horses sitting just behind him — particularly those with some prominent-race experience — arrive at the two-furlong pole full of running and with first run.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Concaire's moderate pace is slow enough that he conserves energy and the hold-up horses never generate sufficient momentum to reel him in.
scenarios.body: A gentle early gallop can allow a well-handicapped leader to coast in front and find extra when challenged in the straight, especially over a flat mile where the absence of undulation removes any natural pace injection.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Genuine Closer Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves stronger than anticipated and hold-up horses find clear runs to launch sustained late challenges.
scenarios.body: A faster-than-expected tempo — perhaps triggered by a handful of the redistributed midfielders pushing forward off the break — would stretch the field and create the gaps that a true closer needs; but given how many hold-up types are in this race, traffic at the two-furlong mark remains a serious risk.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Concaire is swamped early by several of the redistributed horses pressing forward and the pace collapses entirely in the straight.
scenarios.body: A scrambled early order with multiple horses vying for prominent spots can produce an uneven gallop that suits neither the leader nor the closers, resulting in a messy finish where the horse with the most residual stamina and clearest passage prevails.

watchPoints.text: Concaire (Ben Coen) is the only genuine front-runner — watch whether he sets a dawdling pace that allows him to coast home or is eventually caught by the chasing pack, as his tempo decision dictates every other scenario in this race.

Oisin Murphy's booking on Zheleznaya Dama stands out in a field of apprentices and mid-tier riders — watch if Murphy positions her far more prominently than her hold-up label suggests, effectively turning her into a pace-tracking threat.

The rear half of this field will be dangerously congested from the start, with nine genuine hold-up horses all seeking the same limited space — watch for significant traffic trouble between the three-furlong and two-furlong poles, particularly affecting Sayonara, Tavarua and Six Wings.

Beau Army (Declan McDonogh) and Cause I Like You (Wesley Joyce) both have placing form at this exact trip and surface — watch whether either jockey elects to push forward and secure a better position than their natural running style would normally dictate.

Stonyfalls's third-place finish at 8f on good ground is the most relevant recent piece of form in the field on a like-for-like basis — watch its market move as a potential dark horse if punters identify the same angle.

races.name: Killarney Plaza Hotel & Spa Handicap

runners_data.name: Spent All Me Money
runners_data.note: A hold-up performer who finished 3rd on good ground over 7f last time; 93 days off is a flag, trainer Adrian Sexton returning at 1/7 over 14 days, and an 8f trip stretches a horse that looks sharper over shorter.

runners_data.name: San Aer
runners_data.note: An 8-year-old hold-up type whose best good-ground form is modest (8th in 15 at this trip recently); the tongue-tie is a familiar piece of kit and Donagh O'Connor's booking brings profile, but a long absence of 64 days and poor recent form make this a difficult proposition.

runners_data.name: Majestic King
runners_data.note: A prominent racer with a genuine win over 8f on good ground in his recent past, though he carries an "fades in finish" flag that is worth noting over a flat mile; trainer Hogan 1/19 over 14 days keeps expectations measured, but the style fit here is genuinely positive.

runners_data.name: No More Porter
runners_data.note: The race's lone front-runner, equipped with tp headgear, and confirmed as the pace-setter in this shape; his good-ground sim record of 0W3P and STYLE_FIT of 0.93 signals he is operating outside his most natural zone, but an uncontested lead is a significant compensating factor.

runners_data.name: Red Hugh O'Donnell
runners_data.note: Running style is unclassified and going is flagged UNKNOWN, making this a real unknown quantity; lightly raced at 5 years old with tongue-tie and bumper headgear, the Paddy Harnett claim is a plus but there is insufficient data to frame a confident view.

runners_data.name: Galley Point
runners_data.note: Returning from 242 days off, which is a major stamina and fitness question; his only similar-going run came in a 10f contest where he finished 9th, and a record of 0W0P in comparable conditions makes this a speculative reappearance runner.

runners_data.name: Tofino
runners_data.note: A genuine prominent racer trained by Gavin Cromwell and ridden by Gary Carroll — a sharp combination; only 18 days since last run and a sim-going record of 1W4P from 15 shows he handles this surface, though his most recent form shows a slide from 2nd to 0.

runners_data.name: Marambo
runners_data.note: Running style unclassified, only three career runs to reference and 207 days absent; all three runs came on standard going at distances of 8f-10f, giving very little to work with for this good-ground mile contest.

runners_data.name: Usuario Amigo
runners_data.note: In strong form last season with a win on good ground, but recent form is a consistent run of 7th-10th placings; a true hold-up horse pushed into a midfield map position here, having run just 3 days ago, and the STYLE_FIT tag reflects the difficulty of securing a true closing run from this field shape.

runners_data.name: Amemri
runners_data.note: David Marnane's 6-year-old has a solid foundation — a course win on good ground and a 2nd at 8f — but the visors and the redistribution away from his natural deep hold-up position undercut the advantage; STYLE_FIT of 0.93 is honest about the mismatch between his preferred role and what this race shape delivers.

runners_data.name: Elusive Duke
runners_data.note: Ridden by Oisin Murphy, whose presence lifts profile considerably; a prominently raced type with five placed efforts from 14 similar-going starts, and back-to-back 2nd-place finishes in his recent history suggest a horse in consistent form who suits this pace structure well.

runners_data.name: Hexagonal
runners_data.note: Chris Hayes takes the mount on a horse whose true nature is as a hold-up closer, pushed into a midfield slot on this map; his tb headgear is familiar equipment, sim-going record of 0W1P is moderate, and the STYLE_FIT warning of 0.90 is the lowest in the field — this horse faces the biggest style compromise.

runners_data.name: Mythical Rock
runners_data.note: Ben Coen partners a prominent racer for the in-form C Byrnes yard (3/10 over 14 days); sim-going form of 0W2P from 15 comparable runs is modest, but the trainer angle and the style fit make this a horse worth watching through the early stages.

runners_data.name: Mags
runners_data.note: A habitual hold-up performer with a deeply poor recent record — four blanks on good ground, including a 20th in an 8f handicap; the redistribution onto the midfield map is telling, and despite the one win on standard at 8f, there is little evidence this horse can improve in this company.

races.paceDynamic: No More Porter is the one confirmed front-runner in a 15-runner handicap, and with no genuine challenger for the lead, he should be able to dictate a controlled, honest gallop from the front without being pressured into a destructive pace. Majestic King, Tofino, Mythical Rock and Elusive Duke are the main prominent-tracking types likely to sit just behind him in the early order, giving the race a reasonably compact shape through the first half of the mile. The field carries more hold-up horses than the race map can honestly accommodate — Usuario Amigo, Amemri, Hexagonal and Mags are all true come-from-behind types but are unlikely to get as far back as their natural style demands in a 15-runner field, which blunts their effectiveness. A sustainable, uncontested pace set by a single front-runner over a flat mile on good ground historically rewards horses who travel prominently and can pick up inside the final two furlongs — this race shape clearly favours the prominent-tracking profile over genuine closers, who face a race run at a tempo unlikely to be severe enough to set them up for a winning late burst.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If No More Porter dictates a measured gallop and prominent trackers travel comfortably into the straight.
scenarios.body: No More Porter sets a sustainable pace that plays perfectly into the hands of horses able to track him closely through the race, with the prominent types quickening off a steady tempo inside the final two furlongs; Majestic King and Elusive Duke are best placed to exploit this shape, travelling into contention without burning energy in the early stages.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Late Flurry
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is slower than expected and the field bunches, allowing horses who get closer than usual to produce a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: A falsely run race compresses the field and the finish becomes a sprint in which sharp acceleration over the final furlong decides matters; horses with good top speed and the ability to quicken from a wide position benefit most in this scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If No More Porter, freed from pressure, builds a significant enough lead that he simply outstays the field in the straight.
scenarios.body: Racing on good ground over a flat mile with no rival willing to take him on, No More Porter can control fractions and build momentum that is never fully overhauled; his historical form on good ground (0W3P) tempers confidence but a truly unchallenged lead changes his profile meaningfully.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent horses are drawn into a faster-than-expected pace battle or check in the straight, opening a gap for closers to swoop.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires genuine pace and traffic trouble for the leaders, conditions that are unlikely given the single front-runner template and the redistributed nature of the closers in this field; Usuario Amigo and Hexagonal would be the theoretical beneficiaries, but both are racing out of their natural deep hold-up role.

watchPoints.text: No More Porter's ability to hold his lead into the straight is the pivotal tactical question — if Majestic King or Tofino press him in the first half-mile, the pace lifts and the shape shifts entirely away from the front-runner.

Elusive Duke and Oisin Murphy could be significantly underestimated — Murphy rarely takes a ride without intent, and a horse placed five times on similar going tracking a controlled pace is dangerous if overlooked in the market.
Galley Point returns from 242 days off and has no comparable good-ground form at this trip — if he bounces wide or unbalances the pack early, he could disrupt the expected compact early order.

Usuario Amigo ran just 3 days ago and is now mapped to midfield despite being a genuine hold-up type — monitor whether McDonogh attempts to slot closer than expected, which could signal a more aggressive ride than the style data suggests.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses (Amemri, Hexagonal, Mags, Usuario Amigo) all racing out of natural role means the final furlong could be more compressed than the pace map implies — their inability to get truly deep could paradoxically close the gap with the prominent types at the death.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Handicap

runners_data.name: Ankara
runners_data.note: Long absence of 267 days is a major concern; Joseph O'Brien string in solid 15/44 form but this hold-up specialist has a worrying tendency to fade in the finish and her best form has come over shorter trips at the Helix.|

runners_data.name: Spanish Temptress
runners_data.note: Ran well for a debut win over 8f on soft before building through the trip to 10f, and her most recent second at 10f on good ground is directly relevant here; Chris Hayes in the plate is a positive, and she's the most battle-hardened prominent type in the field.|

runners_data.name: Diamond Exchange
runners_data.note: Won twice over 10f this season — including on good ground — and her Mrs Harrington yard is 1/29 in 14 days so not firing in volume, but the horse herself is in form and the 5lb claim from Kennedy adds appeal at the weights.|

runners_data.name: Saga Gaga
runners_data.note: The race-shaper: uncontested lead is hers to lose, and her two runs both showed she can roll along in front on good ground over 10f; the concern is that she's only had two career starts, is a 3-year-old stepping up markedly in trip, and leads here out of her natural role per the STYLE_FIT flag.|

runners_data.name: Concert Party
runners_data.note: Not won in any of her 12 career starts on good or good-to-firm ground, and her form figures at the back of the trip range are consistently poor; Mel Sheridan's 10lb claim helps the weight but the hold-up style needs something to chase and she simply hasn't delivered on good ground.|

runners_data.name: Jeaniemacaroney
runners_data.note: A genuine 3-time winner who has scored over 12f and 16f on good ground for McNamara, and her course-and-distance profile is the most directly relevant of the pace-compressed horses; naturally forward-going and capable of forcing the issue if she travels kindly, though the 285-day layoff is a legitimate concern.|

runners_data.name: Forthill
runners_data.note: Ran just two days ago which is an immediate red flag; Paul Twomey's yard is in decent nick at 2/6 but back-to-back race days for a handicapper is unusual, and while she naturally races prominently she is squeezed into a midfield slot here and her STYLE_FIT score of 0.90 tempers expectations.|

runners_data.name: My Girl Grace
runners_data.note: Debut winner over 10f on soft for G M Lyons, who is 5/19 in 14 days and clearly in form; completely unexposed but stepping into handicap company off one run means there is a significant unknown quality — Gary Carroll gives her every chance from a prominent position.|

runners_data.name: So Must I
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's second string, a hold-up type who has recorded a win on standard going and placed at 12f on soft; the 7lb claim from Shay Wallace is useful but her good-ground form reads 6,4,6 and she has shown no ability to quicken from rear on a sound surface.|

runners_data.name: Speckled Meadow
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old veteran who is a natural hold-up horse shuffled into a midfield mapping; her going stats on good ground are modest at 1 win from 15 attempts, and the amateur rider with a 7lb claim does little to offset the concern that this surface and this compressed race shape will find her out.|

races.paceDynamic: Saga Gaga is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, she should stride into a comfortable, uncontested gallop from the front over this 1m3½f trip. Spanish Temptress, Diamond Exchange, and My Girl Grace are the natural prominent types who can track her, meaning the first four or five positions will be occupied early, compressing the midfield. Jeaniemacaroney, Forthill, and Speckled Meadow are all genuinely prominent or hold-up types by nature but are redistributed into midfield slots because there are more pace-seeking horses in this field than the race shape can accommodate at the front — of the three, Jeaniemacaroney's course and distance form gives her the best claim to actually force a forward position if she travels well enough. With Saga Gaga likely to dictate a measured, sustainable tempo unchallenged, this race shape strongly favours horses who can track the pace in the prominent group and quicken from there — hold-up horses coming from genuine rear positions face an uphill task if the pace is never truly injected.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Saga Gaga leads, chasers pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Saga Gaga dictates an uncontested, honest gallop and the prominent trackers fire off her back in the straight.
scenarios.body: Saga Gaga controls tempo throughout and the horses immediately behind her — Spanish Temptress, Diamond Exchange, and My Girl Grace — get a perfect tow into the race, with the best of them quickening past in the final furlong. This scenario rewards the prominent profile most directly and is the dominant shape given Saga Gaga's confirmed pace role and the lack of any serious challenger for the lead.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace collapse, closers strike
scenarios.trigger: If Saga Gaga goes too fast early and fades, leaving a gap for hold-up horses to swoop late.
scenarios.body: A genuinely strong early tempo from Saga Gaga drains the field, and Ankara or So Must I, coming from off the pace, find the straight opening up in front of them. This shape is less likely given the pace is expected to be sustainable rather than pressured, but these hold-up types benefit most if conditions conspire to punish front-runners.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent chaos, front stolen
scenarios.trigger: If Jeaniemacaroney or another redistributed prominent type forces their way to the front and disrupts the expected race shape.
scenarios.body: With several naturally forward-going horses squeezed into midfield, one of them — most plausibly Jeaniemacaroney given her course-winning form — could push forward aggressively and create a busier, more contested early pace. This unsettles Saga Gaga's control and opens the race to a wider range of finishers, potentially suiting Jeaniemacaroney herself if she secures a forward berth.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Dead heat pace, all weaken
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is overly moderate and the field bunches, producing a late sprint that suits the freshest or luckiest.
scenarios.body: A crawl early reduces the race to a sprint finish from the home turn, randomising the outcome and making class and sprint ability the deciding factors rather than tactical positioning. My Girl Grace, lightly raced with a winning debut and trained by G M Lyons, could benefit from this kind of unpredictable lottery.

watchPoints.text: Saga Gaga's inexperience over this trip (1m3½f) is the race's single biggest variable — if she gets it wrong early and sets a false pace, the entire shape collapses and the prominent trackers Spanish Temptress and Diamond Exchange become the primary beneficiaries.

Forthill ran just two days ago and, while Paul Twomey has declared her fit, watch for signs of fatigue in the closing stages — her prominent instincts may see her burn too bright early if she is not at peak freshness.

Jeaniemacaroney returns from 285 days off and, as a naturally forward-going type, there is a real chance she bustles forward early to claim a berth she's not mapped to hold — monitor her early in the race for signs of interfering with Saga Gaga's intended front-running role.

My Girl Grace is completely unexposed having run once, and G M Lyons is in strong 14-day form — a market move in the final hour would be a meaningful signal that connections believe the step up to 1m3½f suits her more than her debut distance suggests.

Ankara's 267-day absence is the longest in the field and her last three runs all came over shorter trips on heavy or soft ground — if the going report confirms a genuinely fast surface at Killarney, her chance looks significantly compromised before the race starts.

races.name: Rose Hotel Handicap

runners_data.name: Tribal Star
runners_data.note: Pace-setter by default in this field; Adrian McGuinness runner has been running prominently but history shows limited wins when on a stamina-testing trip, and the 17-day turnaround is fine — yet the STYLE_FIT flag is a mild caution that this horse is not a natural dominating front-runner, so do not over-rely on the lead translating to victory.

runners_data.name: Persian Bliss
runners_data.note: 71-day absence is a concern for sharpness, but Denis Hogan is capable of producing horses fresh; races prominently and should get a clean run tracking Tribal Star from close range, though a lack of recent racecourse evidence makes it hard to trust fully at this trip.

runners_data.name: Individualism
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse who needs cut in the ground to be at best — sim-going record of 14 runs at similar conditions yielding 2 wins and 5 places suggests good ground is very much in his wheelhouse over distance; W J Lee booking adds confidence, but needs pace to be strong enough to bring him into it.

runners_data.name: Satono Chevalier
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy takes the ride on a horse in fine recent form (three wins from last six, including two at this sort of trip range); races prominently and should slot in just behind Tribal Star naturally — the age (8) is noted but the current form cycle is strong and this is a drop in OR context.

runners_data.name: Sign From Above
runners_data.note: Peter Fahey runner has strong held-up-to-prominent tendencies but will find the space for that role squeezed in this field — sim-going record at the trip shows one win over 20f on soft, and the 50-day gap adds uncertainty; the redistribution means it cannot dictate its own destiny tactically.

runners_data.name: Carthusian
runners_data.note: Mrs Harrington's 4-year-old has been running consistently in mid-to-rear of field on good ground without threatening — a run just seven days ago is a quick turnaround, and the form string of 70797 offers little encouragement; pushed back from its preferred berth, the raw ability to compete at this level looks questionable.

runners_data.name: Gaoth Chuil
runners_data.note: A natural front-runner or prominent type who won at 15f on good last season and placed twice over staying trips in soft-to-good; Chris Hayes gives it a strong jockey booking, but the reality of being unable to push forward freely in this shape is a significant tactical disadvantage — the best case is a well-run race that brings stamina into play.

runners_data.name: Harry's Legacy
runners_data.note: Ross O'Sullivan has fired in three winners in the last 14 days which is worth noting; holds-up and has placed multiple times at staying trips on good, but the 32-day absence and a form string ending in a zero is a negative — needs a genuinely searching gallop to bring his late kick to bear.

races.paceDynamic: Tribal Star is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no horse capable of genuinely pressing them from the outset, is set to control tempo from the front at a comfortable, measured gallop over this 2m1f trip. Persian Bliss and Satono Chevalier will be the horses closest to the pace in their natural prominent positions, while Sign From Above, Carthusian, and Gaoth Chuil — all true prominent types — are pushed back into a midfield cluster they would not naturally occupy, unable to secure their preferred berths against stronger pace rivals. Harry's Legacy and Individualism operate from hold-up positions and will be detached in the early stages, dependent on the race producing enough of a test to reel back the leaders late. With a single uncontested pace-setter dictating a sustainable gallop, this race shape strongly favours horses racing close to the pace — prominent or handy runners who can track Tribal Star without burning petrol and pounce in the straight, rather than deep closers relying on a gruelling pace that simply may not materialise.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tribal Star Controls; Prominent Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Tribal Star leads at a steady clip and the horses tracking them closest have enough left to quicken in the straight.
scenarios.body: Tribal Star sets a sustainable pace throughout, and the horses in genuine prominent positions — Persian Bliss and Satono Chevalier — travel into the race without effort, picking up the front-runner in the final two furlongs; the hold-up horses simply lack the pace injection to close the gap on a non-gruelling gallop.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse; Front Runner Stays
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is so conservative that Tribal Star steals a march and the field never organises a coherent challenge.
scenarios.body: Tribal Star bowls along at such a sedate pace that no one closes the gap until it is too late, and the horse who dictated terms runs out a comfortable winner having never been seriously asked; prominent trackers are unable to quicken past a horse with petrol in the tank.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Strong Gallop Suits Hold-Up
scenarios.trigger: If an unexpected injection of pace — perhaps from a prominent-type pushing forward — lifts the tempo enough to bring late closers into play.
scenarios.body: A faster-than-expected gallop stretches the field and leaves the prominent horses exposed, allowing Individualism or Harry's Legacy to pick up momentum off the bend and finish powerfully through beaten rivals; their strong form at the distance and staying profile becomes a decisive weapon.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Scramble; Redistributed Types Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the redistributed prominent horses — Sign From Above, Carthusian, or Gaoth Chuil — force their way forward early and disrupt the anticipated shape.
scenarios.body: A contested early pace develops as multiple runners push for position, creating a more evenly-run race where a fresh, well-placed horse from the scramble benefits; Gaoth Chuil, who has recent form over this trip range and strong good-ground form, is best placed of the redistributed trio to capitalise.

watchPoints.text: Satono Chevalier (Oisin Murphy) is in a strong form cycle with recent wins and a prominent style that perfectly suits this single-pace-setter scenario — watch for Murphy to slot in second or third early and control his own fate.

Tribal Star's STYLE_FIT flag means the lead may not be as comfortable as it looks on paper — if the horse shows any signs of racing keenly or labours in the closing stages, the door opens quickly for close-tracking rivals.

Gaoth Chuil, Carthusian, and Sign From Above are all naturally prominent horses compressed into midfield — monitor the first two furlongs for any of them forcing their way forward, as a contested early pace would fundamentally change the race shape.

Individualism's chance is entirely conditional on the pace being strong enough to bring a hold-up horse into the race — if the gallop is pedestrian, W J Lee will be powerless to get the horse competitive, regardless of class or trip suitability.

Persian Bliss returns from 71 days off; if Denis Hogan has the horse tuned up, the prominent style fits the race perfectly, but an underdone reappearance would see the horse fade out of contention in the final half-mile of a 2m1f trip.

races.name: Thorn Plant Hire (Q.R.) Maiden

runners_data.name: Ambitious Fellow
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old veteran with solid similar-going form (12/15) and a recent third, but his true hold-up style means he is effectively racing out of role in this field — he needs a strong pace that this race shape is unlikely to generate, and the 36-day absence is a minor query.

runners_data.name: Arch Empire
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's strong 14-day strike rate (10/63) is worth noting, and the horse has placed at distances up to 20f on good ground; his genuine off-the-pace style is compromised by displacement into midfield, where he lacks the natural launch pad a true closer requires.

runners_data.name: Catalani
runners_data.note: Prominent runner for Jack Foley with a recent win at 23f on good ground and place at 22f — the 5-day turnaround is sharp but the horse has shown resilience; sits in a natural tactical position and has the trip form to be competitive if the pace is true.

runners_data.name: Certamen
runners_data.note: Edward Buckley's five-year-old has a modest form line (best effort a sixth) and all five recent runs on similar going have produced zeros; mapped to midfield despite a hold-up tendency, giving it the worst of both worlds in this race shape.

runners_data.name: Chain Of Destiny
runners_data.note: Flagged for fading in the finish and has a worrying form string across varying conditions — the 44-day absence compounds concerns, and this horse's genuine hold-up style sits poorly in a race where the pace is unlikely to set up a late flourish.

runners_data.name: Double Indian
runners_data.note: Mrs Harrington's four-year-old is the youngest in the field and has only three runs on record, all producing modest finishes; the fade flag is a concern over this longer trip, and the seven-day turnaround following a ninth suggests improvement is needed.

runners_data.name: Eagle Fang
runners_data.note: Consistent place-getter with five placed efforts in the last six runs including two seconds, wears a visor (hg:v) and races prominently — the going suits (7/15 on similar), the trip is within range, and the prominent profile is ideally suited to the expected race shape.

runners_data.name: Jetoile
runners_data.note: Eleven-year-old veteran who won at 20f on good ground and has repeatedly placed at this sort of trip; wears a tongue-strap (tp) and has shown the ability to travel prominently, though the modest trainer strike rate (T14: 0/5) tempers expectations slightly.

runners_data.name: Lauro's Legend
runners_data.note: Form reads 7-0 in recent starts and the fade flag reinforces a lack of finishing punch; despite placing once at 16f on good ground historically, P A Fahy's six-year-old has shown little at this level, and the hold-up displacement makes its task harder.

runners_data.name: Lord Ffrench
runners_data.note: S Curling's six-year-old has a win on similar going and consistent placed efforts over 19-22f trips, suggesting the distance and surface are within comfort zone; the 37-day break is not alarming, though the genuine hold-up style is handicapped by the likely race shape.

runners_data.name: Path d'Oroux
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old returning from 75 days off, wearing a tongue-strap and with a form line of just two runs this season showing limited recent evidence; the lengthy break combined with displacement from a natural hold-up position into midfield makes this one to watch rather than rely on.

runners_data.name: Sunny South West
runners_data.note: The race's key pace influence — three wins and three places on similar going confirms suitability, and the hat headgear (hg:h) is noted; the 159-day absence is the only meaningful doubt about whether the horse returns in peak condition, but the style advantage of uncontested lead is significant.

runners_data.name: Ma Belle Etoile
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's seven-year-old has two wins on similar going in 10-14 runs and finished fifth last time out at 12f — the step back up in trip to 1m6f looks a plus given a past win at 16f; the trainer's 14-day form (5/38) is a solid angle, and racing prominently with a light weight (161lbs) is an asset.

races.paceDynamic: Sunny South West is the lone confirmed front-runner in a 13-runner field and, with no genuine rival to press them from the front, is likely to dictate a measured, controlled gallop over this 1m6f trip on good ground at Killarney. Eagle Fang, Catalani, Jetoile, and Ma Belle Etoile are the prominent types who will look to sit just off the leader, creating a compact early section with a small cluster of horses disputing the pace rather than a true tearaway. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than can realistically settle at the rear — Certamen, Ambitious Fellow, Arch Empire, Chain Of Destiny, Double Indian, Lauro's Legend, Lord Ffrench, and Path d'Oroux all carry genuine hold-up profiles but several will be pushed forward into unfamiliar midfield berths, meaning their finishing kicks may be blunted. A controlled, single-pace gallop dominated by Sunny South West favours horses who can travel prominently and sustain their effort — the prominent-to-midfield profile is best placed, with true deep closers facing an uphill task if the pace never truly hotted up.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sunny South West Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Sunny South West dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and the prominent quartet tracks in a tight pack.
scenarios.body: Sunny South West sets a sustainable tempo, the prominent group of Eagle Fang, Catalani, and Ma Belle Etoile travel smoothly in their slipstream, and the race is effectively run to suit those who can quicken from a handy position in the straight; deep closers get little help from a pace they never truly pressured. Prominent horses with strong finishing records on good ground are the primary beneficiaries of this controlled shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Quicken Clear
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent quartet collectively raise the tempo approaching the home turn, stretching the field and stranding the hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: Eagle Fang, Catalani, Jetoile, and Ma Belle Etoile all push up to challenge Sunny South West as the race enters its final stages, injecting a decisive surge that the redistributed hold-up types — already out of their natural role — cannot match from midfield. This shape rewards horses with strong form at this trip on good ground who can sustain a prolonged gallop through the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Genuine Closer Strikes Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough through the middle stages to see the front group tire, allowing a true hold-up horse to finish powerfully.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires the prominent cluster to burn each other out by halfway, opening a gap for a horse like Arch Empire or Lord Ffrench to reel them in down the straight; given how many hold-up types have been displaced into midfield and are unlikely to be in their natural position, executing a clean late run is far from straightforward. Arch Empire's trainer Gordon Elliott is in sharp form (T14: 10/63) and the horse has placed at this trip before, making it the most credible late-closer if the pace genuinely tests the leaders.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Chaos, Field Splits
scenarios.trigger: If the large field of 13 results in positional scrimmaging early, with multiple horses racing against type and the pace fragmenting unpredictably.
scenarios.body: With so many hold-up types displaced into midfield and four prominent runners all jostling for position behind one front-runner, the race could become muddled mid-race, creating gaps and surges that scramble the expected shape; horses with adaptable styles and good form figures at this distance on good ground would be best equipped to capitalise. Catalani, who has placed prominently and has a win at 23f on good ground in recent form, holds residual claims in a muddled scenario.

watchPoints.text: Sunny South West's 159-day absence is the primary race-shaping risk — if the horse returns below peak and fades from the front, the entire controlled-pace scenario unravels and the prominent group faces a very different race.

Eagle Fang, Catalani, Jetoile, and Ma Belle Etoile will all look to press up behind the leader, and if two or more contest for the same ground approaching the first bend in this 13-runner field, early crowding could compromise the prominent runners' positions.

Arch Empire (Gordon Elliott, T14 10/63) is the most credible hold-up threat if somehow a true pace develops — monitor whether the race tempo through the middle stages is strong enough to bring a closer into contention late.

Several hold-up horses — notably Certamen, Chain Of Destiny, and Double Indian — carry fade flags or poor form and are displaced from their natural style; if they loom up mid-race out of position, they risk creating interference without posing a genuine winning threat.

Ma Belle Etoile's lighter weight (161lbs vs 166lbs for most rivals) is a small but concrete edge in a race where condition and stamina are tested over 1m6f — worth tracking if she travels smoothly in the prominent group.
